result: MI induces temporal changes in MMP expression in cardiac macrophages, with Mmp14, Mmp2, and Col1a1 reaching maximum expression at day 7 post-MI, while Mmp9 and Mmp13 are downregulated.
evaluation: Claims C1-C5 are directly supported by qPCR data from sorted cardiac macrophages at multiple time points post-MI (Figure 1A). The temporal expression patterns are clearly demonstrated with appropriate biological replicates and statistical analysis.

result: Macrophage-specific deletion of Mmp14 attenuates cardiac dysfunction and prevents LV dilation after both permanent LAD ligation and ischemia/reperfusion injury.
evaluation: Claims C6, C14-C17, C21-C23 are supported by comprehensive echocardiography data showing improved LVEF, reduced LV volumes, smaller infarct size, and lower WMSI in MAC-Mmp14 KO mice in both MI models (Figures 1B-E, Figure 1—supplement 3A). Multiple functional parameters consistently demonstrate cardioprotection.

result: MAC-Mmp14 KO mice exhibit reduced cardiac fibrosis with less organized, sparser collagen structure after MI compared to WT mice.
evaluation: Claims C7, C18-C20, C24 are supported by SHG imaging and quantitative analysis showing reduced collagen density, increased skewness and kurtosis (indicating thinner, disarrayed fibers) in MAC-Mmp14 KO hearts after both permanent MI and I/R (Figures 1F-G, Figure 1—supplement 3B-C). The structural characterization is thorough and quantitative.

result: MAC-Mmp14 KO mice show preserved cardiac microvasculature with higher vascular density, more capillaries and endothelial cells, improved oxygen diffusion parameters, and reduced hypoxia in the infarct zone.
evaluation: Claims C8, C26-C30 are supported by automated 3D microvasculature analysis (Figure 2A-B, Table 3) and CA-IX staining (Figure 2C-D). The vascular parameters are comprehensively quantified using established methodology (Gkontra et al., 2018), and hypoxia reduction is independently confirmed by CA-IX immunostaining.

result: MT1-MMP activates latent TGFβ1 in macrophages through its catalytic activity, as demonstrated by increased surface retention of LAP-TGFβ1 in MAC-Mmp14 KO macrophages and loss of active TGFβ1 production.
evaluation: Claims C9, C31-C35 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: flow cytometry showing increased surface LAP-TGFβ1 (Figure 3B-C), Western blot of subcellular fractions (Figure 3D-E), unchanged Tgfb1 transcripts (Figure 3F), luciferase assays showing loss of active TGFβ1 (Figure 3G), and rescue with catalytically active but not inactive MT1-MMP (Figure 3H). The mechanistic evidence is comprehensive and internally consistent.

result: Loss of macrophage MT1-MMP reduces paracrine TGFβ1-SMAD2 signaling in endothelial cells, myofibroblasts, and VSMCs in the infarcted myocardium, without affecting macrophage pSMAD2.
evaluation: Claims C10, C36-C40 are supported by flow cytometry (Figure 4B-C) and confocal microscopy (Figure 4D-E) showing cell-type-specific differences in pSMAD2 abundance. The data demonstrate selective paracrine effects on non-macrophage cell types, consistent with the proposed mechanism of MT1-MMP-mediated TGFβ1 activation.

result: MT1-MMP in macrophages promotes endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) via TGFβ1, as demonstrated by reduced transitioning cells in MAC-Mmp14 KO hearts and impaired EndMT induction in co-culture experiments.
evaluation: Claims C11-C13, C44-C53, C61-C62 are supported by multiple lines of evidence: flow cytometry identifying CD31+PDGFRβ+ transitioning cells (Figure 5A-B), lineage tracing (Figure 5—supplement 2), qPCR showing transitional gene expression (Figure 5—supplement 1B), immunofluorescence of ERG+SMA+pSMAD2+ cells (Figure 5—supplement 3C-D), and in vitro co-culture experiments with both BMDMs and cardiac macrophages (Figures 6C-D, Figure 6—supplement 1). Anti-TGFβ1 antibody blocking confirms TGFβ1 dependence. The evidence is comprehensive across multiple experimental systems.

result: MAC-Mmp14 KO mice show altered cellular composition in the infarcted myocardium with fewer macrophages and myofibroblasts but more endothelial cells.
evaluation: Claims C41-C43 are supported by flow cytometry quantification of different cell populations in 7-day post-MI hearts (Figure 5A-B). The changes are consistent with the observed phenotypes of reduced inflammation, reduced fibrosis, and preserved vasculature.

result: Cardiac macrophages from MAC-Mmp14 KO mice retain more surface LAP-TGFβ1 and fail to produce active TGFβ1 after MI.
evaluation: Claims C58-C60 are supported by flow cytometry of cardiac macrophages (Figure 6A) and luciferase assays with sorted cardiac macrophages (Figure 6B). These in vivo-derived data confirm that the mechanism observed in BMDMs operates in cardiac macrophages during actual MI.

result: Mmp14 inactivation does not affect macrophage M1/M2 polarization.
evaluation: Claim C25 is supported by qPCR analysis of M1 and M2 markers in both cardiac macrophages (Figure 1—supplement 4A) and in vitro polarized BMDMs (Figure 1—supplement 4B). This control experiment demonstrates that the observed effects are not due to altered macrophage polarization.

result: The MAC-Mmp14 KO model achieves efficient and specific Mmp14 deletion in macrophages without affecting endothelial cell Mmp14 expression.
evaluation: Claims C81-C83 are supported by qPCR validation of Mmp14 deletion in BMDMs and cardiac macrophages, with no change in endothelial cells (Figure 1—supplement 2D). This validates the specificity of the genetic model used throughout the study.

result: MAC-Mmp14 KO mice show no baseline differences in cardiac function or circulating immune cell populations compared to WT mice.
evaluation: Claims C84-C85 are supported by baseline echocardiography/electrocardiography (Table 1) and hematology data (Table 2, Figure 1—supplement 2B-C). These controls establish that the observed post-MI differences are not due to baseline abnormalities.

result: Co-culture of endothelial cells with WT but not MAC-Mmp14 KO macrophages induces transcriptional changes characteristic of EndMT, including downregulation of endothelial genes and upregulation of mesenchymal genes.
evaluation: Claims C54-C57 are supported by qPCR analysis of co-cultured MAECs (Figure 6—supplement 2). The transcriptional data complement the protein-level observations and confirm the EndMT phenotype at the molecular level.

result: Serpine1 expression is higher in fibroblasts treated with conditioned medium from WT BMDMs compared to MAC-Mmp14 KO BMDMs.
evaluation: Claim C108 is supported by qPCR data (Figure 4—supplement 2A). This finding is consistent with reduced TGFβ1 activation by MAC-Mmp14 KO macrophages and suggests a role for MT1-MMP in myofibroblast activation, though the effect is limited to this single TGFβ1 target gene.

result: The manuscript provides extensive background on MI pathophysiology, macrophage biology, MMP function, EndMT mechanisms, and prior work on MT1-MMP in cardiac remodeling.
evaluation: Claims C63-C110 represent background knowledge and literature citations that provide context for the study. These are appropriately cited and accurately represent established knowledge and prior findings in the field. They support the rationale for the current investigation.
